name: Rocket Companies, Inc.

profile.description: Rocket Companies is a Detroit-based fintech platform spanning mortgage origination, servicing, real estate (Redfin) and personal finance. TTM revenue is about $9.3B (+103% YoY) following the Redfin and Mr. Cooper acquisitions, with Q2 2026 net income of $229M and adjusted EBITDA of $766M [1].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Rocket assembled a vertically integrated home-ownership platform through roughly $16B of acquisitions (Redfin, Mr. Cooper) and a 500,000-listing alliance with Compass [2]. AI Deployment (2/2): management credits AI for Q1 2026 beat on $2.82B revenue and EPS of $0.15 vs $0.12 consensus [1]. Market Share (2/2): largest U.S. retail mortgage lender, now with a top servicing book via Mr. Cooper. Pipeline (1/2): AI-enabled platform integration is ongoing but no dated product launches found. R&D (0/1): no R&D intensity data found versus peers.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): 'Help everyone home' is specific and tied to a larger purpose, shaped by Detroit-centered investment, but has not been proven over decades through crises [2]. Community (1/2): general corporate philanthropy and Detroit revitalization; no dollar figures verified in research. Retention (0/2): no tenure or turnover data found, and the company has had prior layoff rounds. Insider Buying (0/2): no meaningful net insider buying found; founder-controlled structure with periodic share sales.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as Growth on available metrics (5yr CAGR and PEG unavailable). Revenue growth of 91.9% YoY (1.0) and forward P/E of 13.7 (1.0) meet targets [1]. D/E of 140.9% scores 0.69, ROE of 3.0% scores 0.20 (2x weight), and profit margin of 4.6% scores 0.23. Weighted 3.32 of 6 gives 6. Daily dollar volume of about $354M passes the liquidity floor.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): mortgage origination and servicing involve heavy document processing and customer interaction that AI can compress, which could lower origination labor and fee moats industry-wide; Rocket is positioned as an adopter, with an AI-focused CTO, an AI/fintech board member (Alex Rampell) and relationships with Anthropic, OpenAI and Google [2]. Regulation and rate-driven demand remain the dominant earnings drivers, not AI. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI produces efficiency gains but no separately quantified AI revenue.

infinite_game.summary: Rocket has a stated purpose but a cyclical, rate-sensitive business model and a pattern of transformative M&A that reads as scale-seeking. Leadership under CEO Varun Krishna is investing aggressively in technology and talent, though earnings remain tied to quarterly mortgage volumes.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Help everyone home' is a real purpose but reads closer to a business description, and decisions such as the Redfin and Mr. Cooper deals are scale and share driven [1][2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): leadership is building a 'Silicon Valley talent plus Detroit grit' culture and half the leadership team is newly recruited, which signals change more than established trust [2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): competitive language centers on share gains and category dominance; no evidence of rival-as-teacher framing.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): evolved from Quicken Loans to a multi-brand fintech and real-estate platform, but still centered on mortgage.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): the Krishna-led tech overhaul and large acquisitions during a weak housing market were costly long-term bets [2].

investment_thesis: Rocket at $11.70 trades at 13.7x forward earnings after revenue roughly doubled to $9.3B TTM and Q2 2026 delivered its most profitable quarter in four years with $229M net income and $766M adjusted EBITDA [1]. The Redfin and Mr. Cooper acquisitions create an integrated purchase-to-servicing funnel, and AI deployment is credited with margin leverage [1][2].
thesis_continued: The bear case is cyclicality and leverage: Q3 guidance of about $2.6B at midpoint signals deceleration, D/E is 140.9%, ROE is only 3.0% and net margin 4.6%. Integration risk on $16B of acquisitions, rate sensitivity of gain-on-sale income, and AI-driven fee compression across mortgage all cap the multiple, while the stock sits below its 50-day average of $13.37 [1].
key_catalysts: Falling mortgage rates lifting origination volume across an enlarged purchase and servicing base [1]
Mr. Cooper servicing book and Redfin/Compass listing funnel driving recapture and cross-sell [2]
AI-driven cost-to-originate reductions expanding adjusted EBITDA margin beyond Q2's $766M [1]
key_risks: Q3 revenue guidance near $2.6B shows growth decelerating from +93% adjusted revenue in Q2 [1]
Integration and execution risk on roughly $16B of acquisitions with D/E of 140.9% [2]
Rate and housing-cycle reversal compressing gain-on-sale margins; thin 4.6% net margin leaves little cushion [1]
